video_goal: Demonstrate how to cut and invert an Ataulfo mango into a hedgehog shape for easy cubing.
required_subjects_and_props: Golden-yellow Ataulfo mango, small paring knife, wooden cutting board, glass bowl

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands place a bright golden-yellow, oblong Ataulfo mango and a small paring knife side-by-side on a wooden cutting board.
The left hand holds the Ataulfo mango upright on the board, while the right hand positions the blade of the paring knife slightly off-center at the top stem.
The knife slices smoothly down the length of the mango, separating one thick, fleshy 'cheek' from the flat central pit.
The right hand lifts the cut mango cheek off the board, turning the bright orange inner flesh toward the camera.
The left hand cradles the mango cheek skin-side down in the palm, while the right hand brings the tip of the paring knife to the top edge of the flesh.
The knife tip scores three parallel vertical lines down through the flesh, the blade stopping just before piercing the bottom skin.
The left hand rotates the cradled mango cheek 90 degrees to prepare for the next set of cuts.
The knife scores horizontal lines across the previous cuts, creating a distinct crosshatch grid pattern in the bright orange flesh.
The right hand sets down the knife, and both hands grip the outer edges of the scored mango cheek, placing thumbs against the center of the skin underneath.
The thumbs push firmly upward, inverting the skin and forcing the crosshatched mango cubes to fan outward into a spiky 'hedgehog' shape.
The left hand holds the inverted hedgehog mango over a glass bowl, while the right hand uses the paring knife to scrape along the base of the cubes.
The perfectly square Ataulfo mango cubes detach from the skin and tumble down into the glass bowl.
